name: Engine Overheating & Cooling System
disclaimer: Engine overheating can cause warped cylinder heads, blown head gaskets, and permanent engine seizure within minutes.

symptoms: Steam or white vapor escaping from hood
Temperature gauge pinned in the red / 'H' zone
subtopics.criticalWarning: SAFETY CRITICAL: PULL OVER IMMEDIATELY TO A SAFE SPOT AND TURN OFF ENGINE. NEVER OPEN THE RADIATOR CAP ON A HOT ENGINE—pressurized boiling coolant will cause severe third-degree burns!
triageQuestions: Are you currently parked safely, or are you actively driving?
Do you see steam coming out from under the hood?
Do you see sweet-smelling green, orange, or pink fluid pooling under the car?
subtopics.recommendedAction: Emergency pull-over instructions -> Turn off engine -> Allow to cool 30+ mins -> Arrange towing. Do NOT continue driving.

symptoms: Temperature gauge rises in stop-and-go traffic but drops when moving at highway speeds
Heater blowing cold air despite hot engine
potentialCauses: Low coolant level / air pocket in cooling system
subtopics.criticalWarning: Turning on the cabin heater to maximum heat and high fan can act as a temporary auxiliary radiator to pull heat away in an emergency, but immediate service is required.
triageQuestions: Does the temperature normalize once the car is moving faster?
Have you had to top up coolant recently?
subtopics.recommendedAction: Inspect cooling fans, pressure test cooling circuit, check thermostat function.

triageRules: Always instruct immediate engine shutdown when overheating is active.
Categorize vehicle as NON-DRIVABLE to prevent engine replacement costs.
